artifacts.title: Ask a question. Get an answer with sources.
artifacts.summary: Ask a question; Jev chooses retrieval, evaluates evidence and returns an answer or a bounded next step.

artifacts.title: Choose and execute a registered query
artifacts.summary: Jev selects an offered query; delegated preparation and system validation produce executable inputs.

artifacts.title: Prepare and run candidate searches
artifacts.summary: Gather terms, optionally generate five, then run bounded searches and return separate attributable attempts.

artifacts.title: Build once, verify, reuse
artifacts.summary: A proven query gap may produce a reusable capability; unsupported data is not fixed by inventing a query.

artifacts.title: Current implementation and measured proof
artifacts.summary: Current retrieval mechanisms and measured evidence, with the pending decision-store candidate labeled separately.

artifacts.title: Navigate nodes, folders and files
artifacts.summary: Jev chooses observed navigation candidates; the system reads bounded sources and retains the path and evidence.

artifacts.title: How a decision is formed, saved, stored and reused
artifacts.summary: Interpret entity meanings, form a decision with later evidence, then stage, publish and reuse it.

artifacts.title: Forming a decision in a kernel run
artifacts.summary: Recognize entities before intent, split compound requests into approved parts, reuse approved criteria, then you choose.

artifacts.title: Staging the decision record
artifacts.summary: When a run ends, a human-approved decision is written as a YAML record under the run folder, ready to publish.

artifacts.title: Publishing the decision record
artifacts.summary: You run the publish command; the record is validated, written to docs/decisions/, indexed, and merged via git review.

artifacts.title: Retrieving a decision as precedent
artifacts.summary: A later run finds earlier records via the index; Jev judges if each applies, and a strong match asks you to reuse it.

artifacts.title: Leafcutter decision records
artifacts.summary: The canonical Decision dataset for the decision lifecycle: real staged, published and reused kernel decision records, plus an illustrative superseded pair, and the splits (Decomposition) of compound goals, research requests and multi-part questions into bounded parts.

artifacts.title: Approve the generated proposals
artifacts.summary: The kernel's first question after option generation: the options taken from the request (usable as given) and the proposed options, each with what it is grounded in, the proposed criteria marked required or supporting, and the four answers (approve, approve a subset, edit criteria, add an option). Populated from the options and criteria of dec-5e7445182eaec1f2.

artifacts.title: The ranked choice
artifacts.summary: Options ranked by Jev's per-criterion judgement, each with its rank, N of 3 required criteria likely met, required-criteria mean and per-criterion lines with evidence, an explicit note that the ranking is evidence and not a decision, and the choose-one / choose-and-add-a-condition / add-your-own / free-text answers, where the choice decides and the condition is kept verbatim. Populated from dec-5e7445182eaec1f2, where the human chose rank 2.

artifacts.title: Reuse it, or decide anew?
artifacts.summary: The precedent confirm question: dec-ef8ddcb79d668a67 chose Kernel-contract YAML per decision for a matching question; reuse it or decide anew, with the consequence of each choice and why research cannot settle it (only a human may reuse it; precedent is evidence, not authority). Populated from dec-ef8ddcb79d668a67 and dec-7cdc61ea41a206e0.

artifacts.title: Record staged
artifacts.summary: The completed run's result: status completed, the decision and approver, the staged record path, the decisions publish command (the kernel's own interpreter and scripts/run_kernel.py, runnable as printed from any shell) with the publish_folder it writes into, and a note that publishing writes into the repository and is the user's to run. Populated from dec-7cdc61ea41a206e0, staged and never published.

artifacts.title: Published record in review
artifacts.summary: A decision record as reviewed in git or a detail view: title, question, selected option, approval block, precedents considered, supersedes and superseded_by, provenance (run id, Langfuse trace id, repository revision), record path and PR. Populated from dec-d53e1c52cd47c832 (PR #979), with the superseded pair dec-dfb0b8d1eb88ec16 and dec-bcae2c02f17508c1 shown as an illustrative correction, with the condition the human stated on dec-bcae2c02f17508c1.

artifacts.title: Interpret what a retrieval question needs
artifacts.summary: The standalone host interpretation shares public research contracts; its saved model evaluation stays historical.

artifacts.title: Building and curating the criteria library
artifacts.summary: Mined repeat questions become person-approved categories, counted from the records and explorable in Neo4j.

artifacts.title: Leafcutter criterion categories
artifacts.summary: The canonical CriterionCategory dataset: reusable decision-criteria categories mined from published decision records and Langfuse traces, across candidate, staged, published and retired stages, plus the separate Neo4j outcome aggregates keyed by category id.

artifacts.title: Approve the proposed split
artifacts.summary: The human gate for a bundled goal, research request or multi-part question that the kernel offers to split. Two samples: a jev_none goal (reject ends the run blocked) and a bundled_accepted goal of seven parts, where five are offered and two are listed read-only as not covered, ask again (reject keeps it whole). Shows each part with its verbatim span, dependencies and capability, one dropped proposal, and the answers: approve, edit, pick a subset, reject.

artifacts.title: Split progress and report
artifacts.summary: What happens after the split gate. Each part shows its outcome (decided, answered, pending, settled by a human, not settled, not run), its child record link and dependency order. Cards: hand split, mid-run split, research split, a partial run (budget stop, dependants not run, one part still decided), a rejected split kept whole (run not blocked), and a rejected split that ends blocked.

artifacts.title: Atlas flows view and canonical flow URLs
artifacts.summary: The canonical Flow dataset for the Atlas /flows view: real flows with their canonical /flows/<flow id> URLs, how each address resolves (default entry, selected, 404 not-found), step links /flows/<flow id>?step=<step id> that open a step's or branch's drawer (and a 'Step not found' notice for an unknown step), the redirect of legacy /flows?flow=<id>&step=<step> links, the AC drawer's 'Appears in flows' step links, and browser sessions covering select, drill, breadcrumb, back and forward. v2: opening a step's drawer writes ?step=<id> into the address bar and closing it removes it with history replace (no new Back-button entries), so Back and Forward move between flows; selecting or drilling from an open drawer pushes the new flow's URL with no ?step=, and Back restores the drawer that was last replaced into an entry. v3 (owner rulings at the flow gate, so the URL always matches the screen): opening a drawer on bare /flows replaces it with /flows/leafcutter/deliver-a-feature?step=<id>; opening a real step's drawer after 'Step not found' clears the notice and replaces the unknown ?step=; a Source, Kind or Realization filter change that renders a different flow replaces the URL with that flow's canonical URL (no new Back entry), and one that keeps the flow leaves the URL unchanged. Navigation records now carry the filter state and the 'Step not found' notice, and Back and Forward restore an entry's filters.

artifacts.title: Atlas Flows: canonical flow URLs
artifacts.summary: Atlas /flows with canonical URLs: /flows/<flow id> and /flows/<flow id>?step=<id>. Shows shared, default and mock links, step and branch deep links with drawers, 'Step not found', a legacy link redirected (308), 404 'Flow not found' states, AC-drawer links, and history sessions. Drawer open/close writes ?step= with history replace (no Back entries); drill and select push. Open build detail: the drawer scrim blocks a direct drawer switch. From leafcutter/atlas-flows v2.
